requirements.requirement: The shared identity dataops exists on both nodes with UID 4500 and GID 4500.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly resolve dataops to UID/GID 4500 before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared, owned by dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: The directory has numeric ownership 4500:4500 and mode 2770; the effective export grants node2 read-write access, and the NFS server is active and enabled, including after node1 restarted.
Direct findmnt output shows the expected NFSv4 source and target. The fstab entry is present, and the mount recovered after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either node retain consistent dataops ownership and permissions across the share.
requirements.summary: Reciprocal writes were observed from both nodes with ownership dataops:dataops, numeric IDs 4500:4500, mode 660, and intact content. Additional writes and reads succeeded after sequential restarts.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and cross-node behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered identity/service/mount/data state, and successful post-restart I/O. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree with the executor's boot IDs.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not independently inventory accounts, export files, fstab, or directory attributes; those outcomes rely on direct executor command output.
The lifecycle collector found minor retained restart-log residue on both nodes, but no failed services or package inconsistency.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations have clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles: installing NFS support, creating the shared identity and directories, configuring the export, SELinux, firewall, persistent mount, and bounded test files. The failed initial node2 read changed no state before set -e stopped it. No failed services or damaged package state remained. The only unnecessary retained residue identified is /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log on both nodes, incidentally created by the restart commands and not cleaned afterward; the files remained in the final lifecycle snapshot. No unrelated retained mutation was observed.
